title: Approval levels for quotations
pre:
As: MARKETING_MANAGER
Company: ANY
Read "Start here — users & settings" (left menu, top) first.
steps: 1. Sales home → "Set up Sales" → "Who approves, and up to what value": Use the dashed card and "Add this level", three times. Level 1: From 0, Up to 500000, Approved by Branch Manager, For Every business unit. Level 2: From 500000, Up to 2500000, Marketing Manager. Level 3: From 2500000, Up to 0 (= no limit), Business Director. All "In use". The summary above the cards then describes all three in sentences.
expected: 1. Saved without an error; reopening the screen shows what you entered.

title: Check that each Sales test user sees exactly what their role allows
pre:
As: MASTER_ADMIN
Company: ANY
Start here → SET-06 is done: the 19 test users exist, with NO extra permission ticks and nothing ticked on Data scope (except Test SBUHead).
steps:
1. Admin → User register. Find the Sales people: Test MktExec, Test BDM, Test KAM, Test MktMgr, Test BranchMgr, Test BranchMgr2, Test Finance, Test Director.
2. Admin → User register: look at the Role column of every Test user.
3. Open Test BDM → Permissions tab. Change nothing.
4. Open Test MktExec → Permissions tab. Change nothing.
5. Add a person (do not save): pick Role "Marketing Executive", then change it to "Finance", then back.
6. Add a person (do not save): pick Marketing Executive, then tick one extra box, e.g. "Operations dashboard".
7. Sign in as Test MktExec (private window). Look at the left menu.
8. Sign in as Test BDM. Left menu.
9. Sign in as Test MktMgr. Left menu, then Sales home.
10. Sign in as Test BranchMgr. Sales → Quotes.
11. Sign in as Test KAM. Sales → Quotes and Directory → Client register.
12. Sign in as Test Finance. Left menu.
13. Sign in as Test Director. Left menu.
14. As admin: open Test MktExec → Permissions → untick "Sales reports" (View) → Save user. Then sign in as Test MktExec.
15. As admin: open Test MktExec → Permissions → press "Use the Marketing Executive role's access" → Save user.
expected:
1. Each is listed with the role and home office from the Start here table (KAM and BranchMgr2 in Mumbai, the rest in Ahmedabad).
2. No orange "own access" mark next to any of them. (A mark means that person's ticks differ from their role; open them → Permissions → press "Use the … role's access" → Save user.)
3. A green line: "✓ Exactly what the Business Development Manager role gives. The person follows the role…". "Create / edit quotations", "Send quotation to the customer" and "Manage quote follow-ups & reminders" are ticked; Invoicing and the Operations rows are not.
4. A green line naming the Marketing Executive role. "Create / edit quotations" and "Manage quote follow-ups & reminders" ticked; "Send quotation to the customer", "See the inter-office credit figures", Invoicing, Vendors and every Operations row NOT ticked.
5. Each time the ticks change to that role's and the green line names the new role. Press Cancel.
6. The line turns orange: "⚠ Their own access: 1 more than the Marketing Executive role gives…" with a button "Use the Marketing Executive role's access". Press it: the extra tick goes and the line is green again. Press Cancel.
7. Sales, Insights (the Sales dashboard only) and Directory. Not Operations, Money or Quality & Accreditation.
8. Sales, Insights and Directory. No Operations, no Money, no Quality & Accreditation.
9. Sales, Money (profitability), Insights, Directory. Sales home shows the "Set up Sales" and "Document templates" tiles. No Admin, no Quality & Accreditation.
10. Only Ahmedabad quotations. Nothing from Mumbai.
11. Only Mumbai records.
12. Sales (quotations read only), Operations (read only), Money, Insights, Directory (clients and vendors, read only). No Reporting (inspection reports are not Finance's — decision D-07), no Quality & Accreditation, no Admin.
13. Every area; System settings are not offered.
14. Insights is gone from the menu and /crm-dashboard is refused. Open the person again as admin: the tick is still off (it no longer comes back by itself).
15. The green "✓ Exactly what the Marketing Executive role gives" line; Insights is back for Test MktExec.

pre:

steps:

2. Read "Other approvals in Sales".

4. Question "When a quote's value is not covered by any of your approval levels…" — choose "It goes to the approvers of your highest level". Question "May the person who prepared a quote approve it themselves…" — choose "Yes — when it is within their own authority". Question "When a quote needs more than one level, how do the levels approve?" — choose "One after another — level 1 first". Question "If a quote waits too long at one approval level…" — choose "After 1 day". Question "Must a man-month quote come from an approved project costing…" — choose "Yes — an approved costing first". Checklist: "Yes — show the checklist on every quote" and "Yes — every point must be ticked (or waived)". Press "Save these answers".

Page headed "Sales — set up in a few questions" with sections: Approving a quote (it starts with "Who approves, and up to what value" — the levels, editable right here); Approving a deal as it moves stage; Other approvals in Sales; Reviewing the request before it is approved (contract review); Already set by your company's rules.

title: Set approval levels that match a real company — on Set up Sales itself
pre:
As: MARKETING_MANAGER
Company: ANY
Signed in as Test MktMgr (or Master Admin). Start here → SET-07 describes the same three levels.
steps:
1. Sales home → "Set up Sales" → section "Approving a quote" → "Who approves, and up to what value".
2. In the dashed card: Level 1, From 0, Up to 500000, Approved by "Branch Manager", For "Every business unit". Press "Add this level".
3. Look at the new dashed card.
4. Level 2: Up to 2500000, Approved by "Marketing Manager". Add this level.
5. Level 3: From 2500000, Up to 0, Approved by "Business Director". Add this level.
6. Edge: in the dashed card type From 900000 and Up to 800000. Add this level.
7. Change Level 1's "Approved by" to "Business Unit Head" and press that card's Save. Then change it back to Branch Manager and Save.
8. Sales → Quotes → "Approval rules" (the full screen).
9. Edge: in the dashed card type Level 4, From 30000, Up to 100000 (inside Level 1). Add this level.
10. Edge: type Level 1, From 3000000, Up to 0 (a higher range with a lower level number). Add this level.
11. As Test BDM make three quotations — ₹2,00,000, ₹10,00,000 and ₹30,00,000 before tax — and submit each for approval. Open each one's approval steps.
expected:
1. One card per level (Level · From value · Up to value (0 = no limit) · Approved by (role) · …or one named person · For · In use · Save · Remove), and a dashed card at the end with "Add this level".
2. You stay on Set up Sales. A card "Level 1" appears, and the summary above reads "Level 1 — from ₹0 to ₹5,00,000 before tax: Branch Manager."
3. It is already filled in: Level 2, From 500000 — where level 1 stops.

title: A role whose margin is more than 10 points above or below its target margin is flagged — live, on the roles, and for the approvers
pre:
As: BUSINESS_DEV_MANAGER
Company: ANY
PREPARE (about 3 minutes). Do these four things first — the amber warning depends on them.
1) Sign in as Test BDM.
2) Make an enquiry: left menu 🎯 Sales → tile 📨 Inquiries → button "+ New inquiry" (top right). Client: type "TB Refinery" in the Client box and pick "TB Refinery Ltd". Contact person: Ravi Shah. Business Unit: Industrial. Subject: Margin band check. Press "Create inquiry".
3) Make a costing: left menu 🎯 Sales → tile 🧮 Project costing → click "＋ New costing" to open it. In "For — enquiry" pick "INQ-… · TB Refinery Ltd · Margin band check". Leave Basis on "Long — per man-month × BOQ". Press "Create costing". The costing page opens (title "Margin band check", label Draft).
4) Set every loading to 0, so the figures below come out exactly: in the "Settings — loadings, default basis and details" box at the top of the page, type 0 in Overhead %, Insurance %, Bad debt %, Contingency % and Negotiation % (a new costing starts with 8, 0.5, 0, 0.5 and 5). Press "Save settings".
HOW THE WARNING WORKS: it compares a role's margin with the number in its "Margin you want (%)" box. Allowed: that number ± 10 points (a 20% target is fine from 10% to 30%). A role whose "Margin you want (%)" is EMPTY is never checked. The warning never blocks saving or submitting.
WHERE THE WARNINGS APPEAR: (a) while typing — a pale amber strip at the BOTTOM of the "＋ Add a role" form, just under the grey strip of live figures (SALARY · DIRECT COST · LOADED COST · … · MARGIN) and just above the "Add role" / "Save role" button — scroll down to see it; (b) after saving — a pale amber box near the TOP of the page, under the four coloured cards (PROJECT REVENUE · PROJECT COST · PROJECT PROFIT · MARGIN); (c) in the "Team roles" table — "⚠ too high" or "⚠ too low" next to the role's MARGIN figure.
DO NOT PRESS "Work out the CTC and its break-up" in this test: that button rebuilds the salary so the margin comes out exactly at the target — which makes the warning disappear.
steps:
1. Scroll down to the "＋ Add a role" form (under the "Team roles" table). Role: type Inspector. Leave "People for this role" = 1, "Basis for this role" = Long — per man-month × BOQ, "Working days in a month" = 26. Under Price, click the round button "Cost + my margin — the rate follows". In "CTC per person, a month (₹) — to build the salary break-up" type 40000 and press the green button "Build the salary break-up". In "Margin you want (%)" type 20. In "Man-months (BOQ) — all people together" type 12. Do not press "Add role" yet. Scroll down to the grey strip of live figures at the bottom of the form.
2. Still in the same form (nothing saved yet): under Price, click the round button "The client's rate is fixed". A new box "Client's rate, per man-month (₹)" appears; "Margin you want (%)" still shows 20 — leave it. In "Client's rate, per man-month (₹)" type 100000. Do NOT press "Work out the CTC and its break-up". Scroll down to the grey strip.
3. Press "Add role" (the green button at the bottom of the form).
4. In the "Team roles" table, on the Inspector row, click "✎ Edit" (right end of the row). The form at the bottom becomes "✎ Edit role — Inspector", still on "The client's rate is fixed" with 100000 and Margin you want 20. Change "Client's rate, per man-month (₹)" to 42000. Look at the strip under the live figures, then press "Save role".
5. Click "✎ Edit" on the Inspector row again. Under Price, click "Cost + my margin — the rate follows" (Margin you want stays 20). Press "Save role".
6. EDGE — exactly on the line (look only, do not save). Click "✎ Edit" on the Inspector row, click "The client's rate is fixed", and type each of these in "Client's rate, per man-month (₹)" in turn, looking at the strip each time: 57143, then 44445, then 57554, then 44198. Then click "Cancel — add a new role instead" (next to the "✎ Edit role — Inspector" heading) so nothing is saved.
7. EDGE — negotiation padding. In the "Settings — loadings, default basis and details" box at the top, type 25 in "Negotiation %" and press "Save settings". Look at the Inspector row. Afterwards set "Negotiation %" back to 0 and press "Save settings" again.
8. EDGE — a role with no margin set. In the "＋ Add a role" form: Role: Rope access technician. Under Price click "The client's rate is fixed". "Client's rate, per man-month (₹)": 150000. Leave "Margin you want (%)" EMPTY. "Man-months (BOQ) — all people together": 6. Press "Add role".
9. Make the Inspector too high again: "✎ Edit" on the Inspector row → "The client's rate is fixed" → "Client's rate, per man-month (₹)" 100000 → "Save role". Then press "Submit for approval" (in the "Approval" box on the right, below the roles). Sign out (🛡 Logout, top right) and sign in as Test BranchMgr (the level 1 approver). Left menu 🎯 Sales → tile 🧮 Project costing → click the costing's code (AHM/PC/2026-27/…/… Rev 00, title "Margin band check", status "Submitted for approval").
expected:
1. A green note: "✓ Built from a CTC of ₹40,000 a month with your salary components …". Five cost heads appear (Basic, HRA, Special allowance, Provident Fund (employer), Gratuity). The grey strip reads: DIRECT COST ₹ 40,000 · LOADED COST ₹ 40,000 · RATE/MAN-MONTH ₹ 50,000 · REVENUE ₹ 6,00,000 · MARGIN 20.0%. There is NO amber strip under it — the rate follows the 20% you set, so the margin is exactly the target.
2. The grey strip now reads RATE/MAN-MONTH ₹ 1,00,000 · REVENUE ₹ 12,00,000 · MARGIN 60.0%. At once, a pale amber strip appears just under it (above the "Add role" button): "⚠ Margin too high: 60% against the 20% set — 40 points above (allowed: 10% to 30%, before negotiation padding)." If you see no amber strip: check that "Margin you want (%)" still says 20 and that the loadings are 0.
3. The page reloads with a green message "Role added — "Inspector"." Near the top, under the four coloured cards (MARGIN card shows 60.0%), a pale amber box: "⚠ 1 role outside the margin set (± 10 points of the target): • Inspector — Margin too high: 60% against the 20% set — 40 points above (allowed: 10% to 30%, before negotiation padding). Check the cost heads, the fixed rate or the target margin of these roles. You can still save and submit — approvers will see this warning too." In the "Team roles" table, the Inspector row shows RATE 100,000/man-month and MARGIN 60.0% with "⚠ too high" next to it.
4. Before saving, the amber strip reads "⚠ Margin too low: 4.8% against the 20% set — 15.2 points below (allowed: 10% to 30%, before negotiation padding)." After "Save role": the amber box at the top says "Inspector — Margin too low: 4.8% against the 20% set — 15.2 points below …", and the Inspector row shows MARGIN 4.8% with "⚠ too low". (With the default loadings instead of 0 the margin would be below zero — still "too low".)
5. Before saving, the strip shows MARGIN 20.0% and no amber strip. After saving: the amber box at the top is gone; the Inspector row shows RATE 50,000/man-month "@20% marg" and MARGIN 20.0% with no ⚠.
6. 57143 → MARGIN 30.0%, no amber strip (on the upper line — allowed). 44445 → MARGIN 10.0%, no amber strip (on the lower line — allowed). 57554 → MARGIN 30.5%: "⚠ Margin too high: 30.5% against the 20% set — 10.5 points above …". 44198 → MARGIN 9.5%: "⚠ Margin too low: 9.5% against the 20% set — 10.5 points below …". After Cancel the Inspector row is unchanged (20.0%, no ⚠).
7. With 25: the Inspector row shows RATE 62,500/man-month "@20% marg" and MARGIN 36.0% (the 25% padding is added on top of the price) — but there is no "⚠ too high" and no amber box: the check reads the margin before the negotiation padding, which is there to be given away. Back at 0: RATE 50,000 and MARGIN 20.0% again.
8. No amber strip while typing, and after saving no "⚠" on the Rope access technician row and no new line in the amber box — a role with no margin set is not checked, because there is nothing to compare with. (Its MARGIN reads 100.0% because no cost heads were typed for it — that is expected here.)
9. Submitting works normally — the warning never blocks — and the costing reads "Level 1 — Branch Manager (Test BranchMgr): ⏳ waiting — with them now; Level 2 — Marketing Manager (Test MktMgr) — signs last …". Test BranchMgr sees the same amber box near the top: "⚠ 1 role outside the margin set (± 10 points of the target): Inspector — Margin too high: 60% against the 20% set …" — above the "Approve" and "Send back" buttons, so they see it before deciding.

steps:

2. "＋ Add a role" → the Price box.
3. "Cost + my margin": CTC 45000 → "Build the salary break-up", Margin 20, Man-months 12 → "Add role".

title: A submitted costing lists every approval level at the top; only its preparer can take it back

title: Costing the other way round — from the rate the client pays to the CTC you can afford
pre:
As: BUSINESS_DEV_MANAGER
Company: ANY
Signed in as Test BDM. A Draft costing (as SAL-050 up to "Create costing"), basis "Long — per man-month".
steps:
1. "＋ Add a role" → look at the "Price" box.
2. Choose "The client's rate is fixed".
3. Client's rate 66000, Margin 22 → "Work out the CTC and its break-up".
4. Type Role "Site Engineer", Man-months (BOQ) 12 → "Add role".
5. If the costing has a Negotiation % (say 5): repeat step 3.
6. Leave the rate empty → "Work out the CTC and its break-up".
7. Rate 66000, leave Margin empty → build.
8. Set up the "too much" case. Under "Loadings, basis & details": Overhead 8, Insurance 0.5, Bad debt 0, Contingency 0.5, Negotiation 5, and "Loadings applied on" = "Sell rate (Excel-style)" → "Save settings". Then in the Price box make sure "The client's rate is fixed" is chosen — Client's rate 66000, Margin 95 → "Work out the CTC and its break-up".
9. Same, but "Loadings applied on" = "Direct cost (standard)" → "Save settings" → Rate 66000, Margin 95 → build.
10. EDGE · The same numbers in the OTHER question: choose "Cost + my margin", type 66000 as the CTC, Margin 95 → build.
11. A role priced per man-day. In "＋ Add a role" set "Basis for this role" = "Daily deputation — per man-day" (from 14 Nov 2026 each role has its own basis), and in Settings Negotiation 0 → "Save settings". In the Price box choose "The client's rate is fixed" → Client's rate 2800, Margin 22 → "Work out the CTC and its break-up". (Working days in a month: 26.)
12. Change "Working days in a month" to 30.
13. Go back: choose "Cost + my margin", type the CTC the green line gave (52335), Margin 22 → build.
14. EDGE · Do the same two steps with Negotiation 5.
expected:
1. One question with two choices: "Cost + my margin — the rate follows" (chosen) and "The client's rate is fixed". Each figure has ONE box (owner, 14 Nov 2026): "Margin you want (%)", "Man-months (BOQ)", and "CTC per person, a month" with "Build the salary break-up".
2. The CTC box disappears; "Client's rate, per man-month" appears; the button reads "Work out the CTC and its break-up". Never both at once.
3. A green line: "✓ At ₹66,000 a man-month and a 22% margin, you can afford a CTC of ₹… a month. The break-up below adds up to it; the rate is fixed at what the client pays." Heads appear (Basic, HRA, …). The totals strip shows Direct cost = that CTC and Rate/man-month ₹66,000.
4. The role is listed with Rate ₹66,000 and Margin 22% (or a hair above — the CTC is rounded down to a rupee, never up).
5. The rate stays exactly ₹66,000 — the rate you typed is what the client sees, padding included. (The Price box notes the costing's padding.)
6. A red line: "Type the rate the client pays first." Nothing changes.
7. A red line asks for the margin — it decides how much of the rate is left for the person.
8. After "Save settings" the page still has "The client's rate is fixed" chosen (it remembers the last choice). A red line: "At ₹66,000 a man-month with a 95% margin and this costing's loadings (9%), nothing is left for the person's pay. Lower the margin, or check the rate." No heads are built. Why: 95% margin + 9% loadings, both taken from the rate, is more than the whole rate.
9. No red line — the sum still works: 5% of the rate is left (₹3,300), less the 9% loadings on top of the pay, gives a CTC of ₹3,027 a month. The rate stays ₹66,000. (Tiny, but not impossible, so it is not refused.)
10. This takes 66,000 as the person's salary, not the client's rate. No red line: the rate becomes 66,000 + 9% loadings = 71,940, ÷ 5% = 14,38,800, + 5% negotiation = ₹15,10,740 a man-month. Correct arithmetic for a 95% margin — this is what the owner saw on 13 Nov 2026 when the page had reopened on the CTC question.
11. The rate box reads "Client's rate, per man-day". Green line: "At ₹2,800 a man-day and a 22% margin, you can afford a CTC of ₹52,335 a month." The CTC is always a MONTH's. The heads and the strip below are per man-day (this sheet is priced by the day) — and the strip shows the month beside them: "Salary /man-day ₹1,877.53 = ₹48,816 a month", "Direct cost /man-day ₹2,012.88 = ₹52,335 a month" — the same ₹52,335 as the green line. Rate/man-day ₹2,800. (Overhead 7.5, Insurance 0.5, Contingency 0.5, loadings on the cost; other loadings give other figures.)
12. The month stays ₹52,335 — the salary is a month's. The day figures fall at once: Direct cost /man-day ₹1,744.50 (52,335 ÷ 30), Salary /man-day ₹1,627.20. The rate stays ₹2,800 (it is what the client pays), so the margin goes up. Set it back to 26.
13. The rate comes out at ₹2,800 again (within a rupee) — the two questions agree.
14. Client's-rate question: still ₹2,800 (the rate typed is the rate quoted). Cost + margin question: ₹2,940 — that is ₹2,800 + 5%. They differ on purpose: with "The client's rate is fixed" it is final, so the 22% is earned on ₹2,800; with "Cost + my margin" the 22% is protected and the 5% padding is added on top, to give away in negotiation.

title: A costing cannot be unlinked once its quotation has gone for approval, been approved, sent, won or given a contract
pre:
As: BUSINESS_DEV_MANAGER
Company: ANY
Signed in as Test BDM. An APPROVED costing linked to a Draft quotation (SAL-052).
steps:

title: Sales approvals in one place — and the contract rule set by the company
pre:

10. Tick a role nobody holds (and nothing else) for the final approval → Save.
11. Choose "…and/or one named person" = Test BranchMgr → Save.
12. Untick everything and choose "— nobody by name —" in both boxes → Save.
13. Sign in as Test MktMgr (may approve quotations, may not change company settings) → Admin → Approvals → Sales → Contract.
14. Left menu → Sales → Set up Sales.
15. Left menu → Admin → Company setup.

1. A card and a tab "🎯 Sales" beside Recruitment, Quotes & reports, Delegation.
2. "Sales approvals" with five tabs: Quotation · Project costing · Contract · Deal stages · Leads. Each tab says the rule in force in plain sentences.
3. The approval levels (each editable in place), and the questions: value not covered by a level, self-approval, one after another / together, escalation.
4. States that a costing uses the quotation levels and is never approved by its author; one question: must a man-month quotation come from an approved costing.
5. The rules in force as sentences; "Add or change the rules for deal stages →" on Deal stages. Leads has nothing to change (its rules are fixed today).
6. "Today: two signatures — first Operation Manager, Business Unit Head, Admin, Business Director or anyone who manages a branch's users, then the final approval from Branch Manager or Branch Application Manager (two different people)." Below: "How many approvals…?" (Two / One / None), "…may one person give both?", and two boxes "Who gives the first signature?" / "Who gives the final approval?" with the roles ticked and "Can sign today: <names>".

8. Both signer boxes disappear.
9. Message "Saved — Final approval → Finance. It applies from now on." The first line now reads "… then the final approval from Finance", and a note "This is your company's own rule. The standard one is: …".
10. A warning line: "⚠ Nobody can give the final approval yet — no active person holds it (…). Until someone is, only the Master Admin can sign."
11. That person is listed under "Can sign today" and is offered the approval on a waiting contract.
12. The standard rule is back.
13. The rule is shown with "🔒 This rule is changed by someone who may change the company settings"; the choices are greyed. The Quotation tab is still editable for them.
14. The same sections on one page — a change made in either place shows in the other.
15. A card "Approvals — Who signs off quotations, costings and contracts — the standard rules, or your own" leads to the same screen.

Then the final approval — <names>." and, in bold, "You give the final approval, after the first signature. (You can give the first signature instead — but then someone else must give the final approval.)" with a quiet button "Give the first signature instead".

3. "First signature given. Waiting for the final approval — <Branch Managers by name>."

pre:

18. Page 'Work order …' with Stage · Target · Actual · Status. Work order register row: Client ZZ FLOW1, Executing Office yours. Contract page 'Work orders raised under this contract' lists it. Note the WORK ORDER NO.
19. Only valid next steps offered; status moves; history kept.

30. Not available to the Coordinator — only Accounts issues.

35. Inspections 1, Closed 1, Revenue ₹25,000 — same as Profit by work order.
36. The invoice row shows party ZZ FLOW1, GSTIN/place of supply, Taxable 25,000, CGST+SGST (same state) or IGST (other state), Total 29,500; the receipt appears in Receipt vouchers with TDS 500. (Use '⬇ Tally XML (import this)' only when really handing over — it is recorded under 'Batches already handed over'.)

title: Quality loop: complaint → nonconformity → corrective action → closure → management review
pre:
As: several
Company: ANY
Test logins (Admin → User register → + Add a person, all in one office, e.g. Ahmedabad): zz.bdm (Business Development Manager), zz.mm (Marketing Manager), zz.fin (Finance), zz.om (Operation Manager), zz.bm (Branch Manager), zz.co (Coordinator), zz.ins (Inspector, linked to a team member), zz.srins (Senior Inspector, set as the inspector's approver in Admin → Approvals → Approver mapping). Also zz.qh (Quality Head). FLOW-01 done (JOB NO and IRN exist).
steps:
1. [Coordinator] Left menu → Quality & Accreditation → Complaints & appeals → 'Record one'. What is it? = Complaint; Received on = today; How it reached us = E-mail; Who from = Client; Their name = Ravi Flow; Which client = ZZ FLOW1 Engineering Pvt Ltd; Which team member = the FLOW-01 inspector; Job number = JOB NO; Report number (IRN) = IRN; Subject = ZZ FLOW3 report issued late; What they told us = 'Report came 8 days after inspection'. 'Record it'.
2. [Coordinator] Handle → '1 · Acknowledge' → 'Record it'; '2 · Is it ours to answer?' → 'Save'; '3 · Investigate' → findings → 'Save findings'.
3. [Coordinator] Quality → Nonconformity workspace → NCR register → '+ Raise a nonconformity'. What was wrong = ZZ FLOW3 report late; Where it came from = A complaint; Reference at the source = CMP NO; Major; Against a job = JOB NO; Owner = Quality Head; Due by blank. 'Raise it'.
4. [Quality Head] NCR → '1 · What was done immediately' → text → 'Save'. '2 · What happened to the work that was already wrong' = Correct and re-issue the document → 'Record it'.
5. [Quality Head] Try '4 · Close it' now.
6. [Quality Head] '3 · Does it need a corrective action?' → 'Open a corrective action from this'.
7. [Quality Head] CAPA → '1 · Cause': Root cause, How it was worked out = Five whys, elsewhere = No — we looked… → 'Save'. '2 · Plan' → What will be done, Whose job, By when → 'Save plan'. '3 · It was done' → Carried out on = today → 'Record it'.
8. [Coordinator] Try '5 · Close' on the CAPA.
9. [Quality Head] '4 · Did it work?' = Yes — it worked → 'Record the check'. '5 · Close' → 'Close …'.
10. [Quality Head] NCR NO → '4 · Close it'.
11. [Master Admin — not involved in the case] Complaint CMP NO → '4 · Decide' → 'Record the decision'. Check 'Who may not decide this'.
12. [Coordinator] Complaint → '5 · Tell the complainant' → Save; '7 · Close' → Close.
13. [Quality Head] Open Quality & Accreditation → Management review.
14. [Master Admin] Management review → 'Hold a review': Held on = today, Period from = first of this month, to = today, Chaired by = Rahul Desai. 'Open it'.
15. [Master Admin] Press 'Re-count from the system'.
16. [Master Admin] 'Record a decision': About = The management system and its processes; Whose job; By when; The decision = 'Report TAT alert at 5 days'. 'Record it'. Then 'Complete the review'.
17. [Business Director] Insights → Analytics & performance → 'Quality' view, this month.
expected:
1. Complaint page 'CMP-… — ZZ FLOW3 report issued late', tabs Overview · Handle · History. Register row with Received date. Note CMP NO.
2. Each step dated in 'What happened, in order'; register shows the acknowledgement date within the 'Acknowledge within (days)' deadline.
3. NCR page 'NCR-… — ZZ FLOW3 report late', 'Major Open A complaint'; Due date = 14 days from today (blank = 14 days if major). Note NCR NO.
4. Both recorded with name and date.
5. Refused — 'Before this can be closed' lists the missing corrective action (a major one cannot be closed without one).
6. CAPA page 'CAPA-… — …' 'Major · raised today · A nonconformity'; 'Quality case — the full story (2 linked)'. Note CAPA NO.
7. Each step recorded in 'What happened, in order'.
8. Not offered / refused (closing a corrective action needs capa.close — Quality or Technical Head).
9. CAPA status Closed. (Choosing 'No — it did not' instead offers 'Close as ineffective and raise a further action'.)
10. NCR Closed with closure date; register Status Closed.
11. Decision recorded; the inspector and the recorder are listed as people who may not decide. Note: by default only administrators hold 'Decide complaints and appeals' — the Quality Head cannot decide. Record as a gap for the owner (who should decide complaints).
12. State closed; register columns Outcome, Decided by, Told filled.
13. Expected for the owner's quality role: opens. Today the Quality Head holds no 'Internal audits & management review' right by default — if refused, record as a gap and continue as Master Admin.
14. Review page 'MR-… — management review' with 'The required inputs (§8.9.2 — all 15)'.
15. The complaints, nonconformities and corrective-action inputs count CMP NO, NCR NO and CAPA NO.
16. Decision row in 'What came out of it'; review State completed; Management review list shows Decisions 1.
17. 'Open nonconformities' does not include NCR NO; 'Average NCR closure time' includes it; 'CAPA effectiveness' counts CAPA NO as effective.

title: A company that needs people creates an account and posts a requirement
pre:

expected:

(ticks in four groups: Inspection & Technical Services, Resource Supply, Recruitment, Project Services) and "Set me up automatically — based on what I ticked above (recommended)"; 3 Your name, Work e-mail, Mobile, "Choose a password". Button "Create my account →".

pre:

title: Newly opened contracts show from their start date to their end date; a coordinator can put one aside until a date
pre:
As: COORDINATOR
Company: ANY
Three OPEN contracts with no work order: A started last week, B starts in 40 days, C ended yesterday. Signed in as a Coordinator.
steps:
1. Operations → Raise a call (or the dashboard tile "contracts opened — raise the call").
2. Under A open "No work yet — remind me later" → pick a date 10 days ahead → note "Work after the shutdown" → Put aside.
3. Try a date of today, or one after the contract's end date.
4. "Back on the list now" beside A.
5. EDGE · Wait for the date (or ask an admin to move it).
expected:
1. "Newly opened — no call raised yet" lists A only. Below it, "Starting later" lists B with its start date. C is not shown — it ended without work.
2. "Put aside — it comes back on the list on <date>." A moves to "Put aside" with the date, the note and your name; the dashboard count drops by one.
3. Refused: "Pick a date after today." / "The contract ends on … — pick a date before then."
4. "Back on the list." A is on the list again.
5. On that date A returns to the list by itself.

title: FLOW — complaint → investigation → nonconformity → corrective action → closure
pre:
As: several
Company: ANY
Logins: Coordinator, Master Admin (decides complaints), Quality Head. A TEST client and a TEST job. Use records whose title starts with "TEST –" so they are easy to find and close afterwards.
steps:
1. COORDINATOR: Left menu → Quality & Accreditation → Complaints & appeals → "Record one": Subject "TEST FLOW – wrong DFT on report", description, client, job number. "Record it".
2. COORDINATOR: Handle → 1 · Acknowledge → "Record it".
3. MASTER_ADMIN: Handle → 2 · "Ours to answer…" → Save; 3 · Investigate → findings "DFT readings mis-typed" → "Save findings".
4. MASTER_ADMIN: 4 · Decide → "Upheld — the complaint was justified", reasons → "Record the decision".
5. MASTER_ADMIN: 6 · Corrective action → "Raise a nonconformity from this".
6. COORDINATOR (or the same admin): choose Major, "Raise it".
7. QUALITY_HEAD: open the NCR → containment "report recalled" → Save; disposition "Correct and re-issue the document" → Record it.
8. QUALITY_HEAD: "Open a corrective action from this".
9. QUALITY_HEAD: on the CAPA record cause (Five whys), plan, "It was done", then "Did it work?" = Yes with what you looked at; "Close CAPA-…".
10. QUALITY_HEAD: back on the NCR → close it.
11. MASTER_ADMIN: complaint → 6 · record the CAPA reference if not already linked; 5 · Tell the complainant → "Record it"; 7 · Close.
12. Open the three registers (Complaints, NCR, Corrective actions).
expected:
1. Complaint CMP-2026-… created.
2. "Acknowledged. That is the first date an assessor looks at."
3. "Recorded: Ours to answer…"; "Saved."
4. "Decision recorded. We found fault, so a corrective action is now needed before this can be closed."
5. The Raise a nonconformity form opens pre-filled: title "Complaint upheld: TEST FLOW – wrong DFT on report", source a complaint, the job and client carried across.
6. NCR-2026-… raised, status Open.
7. "Containment recorded."; "Disposition recorded."
8. "Corrective action opened, carrying everything already recorded here."
9. "Closed, and verified effective."
10. "Nonconformity NCR-… closed."
11. "Recorded that the complainant was told, and when."; "Closed."
12. All three TEST FLOW records are Closed and link to each other; each History lists who did what and when.

title: FLOW — report drafted → vetted → approved → issued → client acceptance → revision → release note
pre:

steps:
1. INSPECTOR: Left menu → Reporting → New report → Load the TEST work order → type IR → Approver = the Branch Manager → "Generate report".
2. INSPECTOR: "✍ Fill report" → fill fields; on Technical writing convert "visual ok" and paste it into the observation field; add site photos; save.
3. INSPECTOR: "✓ Submit for review".
4. BRANCH_MANAGER: open it → "↩ Return for correction" with note "TEST – add photo captions".
5. INSPECTOR: fix and submit again.
6. BRANCH_MANAGER: tick checklist → "✓ Vet (cleared)".
7. BRANCH_MANAGER: "✓ Approve".
8. BRANCH_MANAGER: "Finalize & issue".
9. OPERATION_MANAGER: "Finalize & issue" → OK.
10. COORDINATOR: Quality & Accreditation → Client acceptance.
11. COORDINATOR: on the report "♻️ Reissue as new revision".
12. COORDINATOR: on the issued original "📋 Draft Release Note".
13. Open the Audit tab and Audit log.
expected:
1. "Report created — IRN …" Status Draft.
2. Saved; completeness checks pass.
3. "Report submitted — sent to the vetting authority. Once vetted it goes to the approver automatically." Status At vetting.
4. "Report returned to the inspector for correction." Status Draft.
5. At vetting again.
6. "Report vetted and forwarded to the approver automatically (1 level)." Status Under review.
7. "Report fully approved — it can now be finalized & issued." Status Approved.
8. Refused: approver and issuer cannot be the same.
9. "Report <IRN> finalized & issued. It is now locked (immutable)." 🔒
10. The IRN is listed under "Issued, no answer yet" with Waiting 0.
11. "Revision drafted as <IRN>/R1 …" — the original stays Issued.
12. "Release Note … drafted from <IRN>…"; listed in Release Notes.
13. Every step with who, role and when.

title: FLOW — billable event → invoice → receipt → reconciliation → month-end cost run → profit by work order → Tally
pre:
As: several
Company: ANY
Run on the test copy (14-LIVE-CHECKS-GUIDE Part 7) or against a TEST customer only: issuing an invoice uses the next number in the branch's GST series and can never be deleted — only cancelled. Amounts on screen are shown to the whole rupee; the Print / PDF shows paise. Logins: Coordinator, Finance, Master Admin. A TEST customer in our state; a TEST job of 2 man-days at ₹8,000 closed this month.
steps:
1. FINANCE: Left menu → Money → Billable events → "⟳ Sync from closed work" → "Approve" on the TEST job.
2. COORDINATOR: Left menu → Money → Billing workspace → month = this month → tick the TEST job → "Draft invoice for the ticked work".
3. COORDINATOR: look for "Issue it".
4. FINANCE: open the draft → "Issue this invoice" → OK.
5. FINANCE: Billable events → Status "Billed" after "⟳ Sync".
6. FINANCE: 💰 Money in → record ₹18,560 with TDS ₹320 (2% of ₹16,000) → "Match it" against the invoice.
7. FINANCE: ⏳ Ageing.
8. FINANCE: Revenue reconciliation.
9. MASTER_ADMIN: Office costs & overheads → save the month; Month-end cost run → "Calculate and store <Month>".
10. FINANCE: Profit by work order → this month → TEST job.
11. FINANCE: Business Unit profit & loss → this month.
12. FINANCE: 📤 Export → Sales vouchers for this month → "Show" → "⬇ Tally XML (import this)"; then Receipt vouchers.
13. MASTER_ADMIN (end of month): Month-end cost run → "Close the month".
expected:
1. "Billable event approved to bill."
2. "Draft invoice started. Check the lines, then issue it." Line: 2 × ₹8,000 = ₹16,000; GST ₹2,880; total ₹18,880.
3. Not offered (Raise only).
4. "Invoice issued. It is now in the customer's ledger and in the ageing." Number allocated.
5. The TEST event shows Billed with the invoice's own line before tax (₹16,000), not ₹18,880.
6. Invoice Paid: ₹18,560 + ₹320 = ₹18,880; Still outstanding ₹0.
7. The invoice no longer appears as owed.
8. The TEST job is not listed (figures agree).
9. "₹<total> allocated for <Month>."
10. Revenue ₹16,000 (before GST); costs listed; Profit = Revenue − Total cost.
11. The TEST job's revenue is included in its unit.
12. Both batches recorded; Tally accepts them; showing again lists nothing new.
13. "<Month> closed. The figures are fixed now …"

title: Screen check — Welcome — let’s set up your system
pre:

Company: ANY
Signed in as the Master Admin. Screen address: /setup
steps:
1. Open the screen: Go to Welcome — let’s set up your system (or type /setup after the site address).

description: Contract registration & approval lifecycle (incl. partner-screen contract-add, PENDING -> endorsement -> approval)
v51: Fixed in V51 — PROVISIONAL, from reading the code only; to be confirmed by a live test
evidence:
Recorded open: phpapp/PENDING.md:49-52 (R4 residual). Recorded closed later: docs/99-gaps-and-risks.md:84-88 ('Lifecycle door closed (Revamp P5b)'). The two documents disagree; PENDING.md is stale.
Partner-screen door in v51.1: phpapp/index.php:1616-1627 requires licence_module_live('quotes') and can('crm.contract.register')||is_master(); after the INSERT, index.php:1751-1762 sets open_status='PENDING', is_active=0, records branch/requester and calls contract_after_register(). Same lifecycle as the CRM path.
CRM door: phpapp/lib/crm.php:3223-3233 (quote-contract) requires crm.contract.register and an ACCEPTED, current revision (SA-09/10); new contract INSERTed directly as 'PENDING' (crm.php:3308) then contract_after_register(). Group contracts crm.php:1025 and deal contracts lib/opportunities.php:895 also INSERT 'PENDING'.
Lifecycle: lib/contracts.php:1200-1262 ops_contract_open - endorse requires can_endorse_contract_open() and status PENDING; approve requires can_approve_contract_open(), the first signature when two are configured, and a different person unless contract_same_person=yes (contracts.php:1239-1252); reject/reopen (reopen only from CLOSED/REJECTED, 1265-1283); amendments to an OPEN contract take the same signatures (1287+, D-25).
Configurable rule: lib/contracts.php:749-765 contract_open_rule() - setting contract_open_signatures 0/1/2 (default 2); with 0, contract_after_register() (contracts.php:899-905) opens the contract at registration. This is the owner's documented rule (docs/02-permission-matrix.md:286), not a defect, but it means 'two signatures everywhere' is a configuration, not a guarantee.
Observation 1: index.php:1734-1756 inserts with the column default open_status='OPEN' (lib/contracts.php:47) and then flips to PENDING inside try{...}catch(Throwable){} - if that UPDATE fails the contract stays OPEN and live. The CRM paths avoid this by inserting 'PENDING' directly.
Observation 2: the /contract-openings queue (lib/contracts.php:1172-1183) lists every PENDING contract with no branch filter, and ops_contract_open endorse/approve (1217-1252) checks role/signature holders but never scope_allows() against partner_contracts.branch_id; contract_sig_people() (805-817) only ranks names by branch. A Branch Manager of one branch may therefore be able to approve another branch's contract (cf. SA-06, fixed for quotations only).
Observation 3: quote-contract re-uses an existing contract with the same number for the same client and keeps its open_status (crm.php:3303-3305) - intended draw-down, but a CLOSED/REJECTED one is linked as-is.
Tests: phpapp/tests/test_contract_backdoor_guard.php:41-45 is a source-text (strpos/regex) check, not a behavioural test; behavioural coverage in test_contract_open_rule.php, test_contract_openings.php, test_sales_contract_amendment.php, test_opp_direct_win_contract.php, test_quote_group_contracts.php.

Then as a Branch Manager of branch B open /contract-openings and try to approve a branch-A contract (expected: refused; if it succeeds, defect). Check Admin -> Approvals -> Sales -> Contract shows 'two approvals'.

description: Possible duplicate cost recording: job-closure expenses vs inspector vouchers
v51: Reproduced in V51 — PROVISIONAL, from reading the code only; to be confirmed by a live test
evidence:
Recorded: phpapp/PENDING.md:53-55 (R9 'left as-is'); docs/99-gaps-and-risks.md:152-160 ('Convergence ... still open'); docs/audit-2026-10/07-DASHBOARD-AND-KPI-AUDIT.md:220-224.
Write path A (coordinator, job closure): phpapp/lib/ops.php:8735-8747 (INSERT at 8742) INSERT INTO expenses (travel, local, food, lodging, misc, extra) - now once per job (field finding #21 guard at 8740).
Write path B (inspector voucher): voucher_entries rows (row_total) written in ops_vouchers (phpapp/lib/ops.php ~7775-8125, voucher-save/voucher-entry).
Readers that add both sides: job_profit() phpapp/lib/ops.php:2502-2506 ($expenses = job_expenses_total + $voucher = job_voucher_total) and 2526 ($direct = ... + $expenses + $voucher ... - $dedupe); job_voucher_total() ops.php:2598-2600 sums row_total with NO voucher-status filter (DRAFT/rejected lines count); boss_profit() ops.php:9154-9201 (unified path via job_profit; legacy path 9194 + 9197 sums expenses + all voucher row_total by boss_id with no de-dup); call register cost column ops.php:5511-5512 and call_cost_incurred() ops.php:6222-6229 add both with no de-dup; SBU P&L lib/costing.php:753-762 folds voucher into expenses in unified mode. The month-end cost run (lib/costing.php:325-345 costing_inspector_days) uses voucher days for labour allocation, not reimbursables.
Guard: lib/costing.php:990-1031 cost_sources()/cost_dualwrite_* detector (flags a job when BOTH totals > 0; overlap = min(); category-blind; only closed jobs; scan limited to last N jobs); warning on job detail views/ops/job_detail.php:1050; amber tile lib/areas.php:266-267; worklist /reimbursable-dedup costing.php:1077-1100; opt-in netting setting reimbursable_dedupe (costing.php:1046-1069) default 'off' = count both.
So by default both doors are still summed in profit, cost-incurred and contract margin; the system warns but does not prevent or net.
retest: On the test copy: close a job entering travel 1,000 at closure; have the inspector add the same trip (1,000) on the monthly voucher (leave voucher in DRAFT). Expect: job Money tab shows the double-entry warning; job_profit cost includes 2,000; /reimbursable-dedup lists the job with overlap 1,000; call register 'Cost incurred' shows 2,000. Switch reimbursable_dedupe to 'net' and confirm profit cost drops by 1,000 while the call-register cost column does not.

description: Role-specific access to Masters and Admin
v51: Reproduced in V51 — PROVISIONAL, from reading the code only; to be confirmed by a live test
evidence:
Recorded: phpapp/PENDING.md:60-68 (R11/R1); docs/99-gaps-and-risks.md:183-199; docs/audit-2026-10/08-GAP-REGISTER.md:529-541 (GAP-005).
Admin rail entry: views/layout_top.php:187-188 shows Admin when ops_area_has('admin') (lib/areas.php:490 = licence ok and >=1 visible tile). Admin tiles lib/areas.php:305-345: Masters tile can('mod.masters.view'); Users/Organisation can('mod.users.view'); Roles & permissions and Role workspaces is_master(); System settings needs mod.settings.view AND settings.manage; Backup/AI settings is_master()||settings.manage.
module_defaults (lib/access.php:859-910): COORDINATOR, OPERATION_MANAGER, SBU_HEAD view 'masters'; BUSINESS_DIRECTOR views ALL modules (incl. users, masters); BRANCH_MANAGER and BRANCH_APP_MANAGER edit 'masters'. Hence COORDINATOR (and BD) see the Admin area - R11 residual confirmed in code.
Generic masters /m/<entity>[/new|edit|delete]: lib/ops.php:3588-3589 maps every m/* route to module 'masters' (needs only mod.masters.view; perm_route_verb() ops.php:3348-3360 returns 'view' for it), then ops.php:3775-3781 master_access_ok($cfg['access']) (ops.php:3263-3268) by TIER: is_admin_level() (MGMT_ROLES lib/access.php:33 = MA, AD, BD, SBU, BM, BAM, OM) or is_coordinator_level(). ops_master_handle (ops.php:4986-4991) deletes/edits with no mod.masters.edit check. description: Custom permission sets - do they stay effective after configuration changes (role edits, module licence changes, cache)?
v51: Reproduced in V51 — PROVISIONAL, from reading the code only; to be confirmed by a live test
evidence:
Recorded: phpapp/PENDING.md:69-70 (R3) and docs/99-gaps-and-risks.md:50-71 (MITIGATED) and :140-141 (R8 BAM residual).
Resolution: lib/access.php:1111-1127 user_effective_perms() - a non-empty users.permissions REPLACES the role set (role_perms() is used only when it is empty). So a later Roles & access edit (ops_access, ops.php ~3720) does not reach a person with their own set, except (a) modules added after the set was saved - merge_new_module_defaults() access.php:1048-1060 using the '@mods=' stamp (1031-1046) or modules_at_last_save(); (b) the four named owner grants pushed into stored sets by access_apply_owner_grants() access.php:1319-1355. user_perms_to_store() (access.php:1155-1175) stores '' when ticks equal the role, so untouched people keep following the role; user_has_own_access() (1180+) flags departures on the user register.
Licence: can() access.php:1445-1447 calls licence_blocks() BEFORE the per-user set and the master bypass, so switching a module off removes it from every custom set immediately, and switching it back restores the stored ticks. licence_blocks() (lib/licence.php:337+) only covers mod.* rights - fine-grained rights such as crm.contract.register or finance.reconcile in a custom set are not licence-blocked by can(); handlers must check licence themselves (e.g. index.php:1623 does).
Cache: ua() access.php:1357-1359 and current_user() lib/helpers.php:176-191 are per-request statics; licence_disabled() lib/licence.php:146-151 per-request with epoch. No session-stored permission snapshot was found, so a change takes effect on the next request.
Custom roles resolve to their base via role_effective_key() (access.php:1113).

Mechanism: phpapp/deploy-check.php (generated, 1,063 lines) carries $RELEASE = '12b7e03 · 2026-11-15 06:04 UTC · 719 files' and an $EXPECT map of size + first 16 hex of SHA-256 for every PHP file (line 27-28 onward); compare loop deploy-check.php:891-899 reports ok / stale / missing; admin-only, 404 otherwise; config-health section 822-889 (which config file supplies DB credentials, sample file with real creds, admin password mismatch). description: The 'someone else saved changes' protection does not work on a work order that has never been edited: two coordinators edit a freshly raised work order, B saves a new required date, A then saves a note from the stale page — A's save goes through and silently puts B's date back.
steps: Coordinator A opens Edit on a new work order; Coordinator B opens Edit on the same one, changes Client's required date, saves; A changes Notes, saves.
expected: A is refused with 'Someone else saved changes to this record while you had it open…'.
actual: A's save is accepted ('Call CALL-00002 updated.'); notes = 'TB edit A' and the required date reverted from B's 16 Nov to the old 24 Nov.
evidence: robot shots/OPS-011-4-fail.jpg
root: phpapp/lib/ops.php:633-643 stale_edit_block() allows the save when the stored updated_at is '' ('no stored version yet → nothing to compare'), and a new call is INSERTed without updated_at (ops.php ~5938). So the first concurrent edit after creation is never protected; the page A holds posts row_version='' as well.
proposal: Set updated_at = row_version_token() when a call (and a job) is created; or treat an empty posted version against a now-non-empty stored version as stale.

description: A manager can move a Cancelled or Closed work order back to an active status with the status Override, although docs/03-object-lifecycles.md says 'The terminal states (CLOSED / REJECTED / CANCELLED) have no exit'.

actual: The Override group offers all statuses; Cancelled → In progress is accepted.

root: phpapp/lib/tosrm.php:493-501 (picker builds the override group from all statuses not in tosrm_allowed_next(), which is [] for terminal ones) and tosrm_set_status() (tosrm.php:207-213) skips the transition check when $force is set.
proposal: Owner to decide: either forbid leaving a terminal status even with override (as the lifecycle says), or document the manager re-open as an allowed transition.

proposal: Warn (or refuse) when the required date is before the received date.

description: Deleting a work order removes the work order and its jobs but leaves its inspection report and its billable event behind, pointing at the deleted work order/job (finding O-F9 / HF-191). The billable event stays 'Pending review' and could still be billed.

expected: The delete is refused while reports / billable events exist, or they are removed/voided with it.
actual: report_docs row (call_id/job_id of the deleted records, deleted=0) and billable_events row (PENDING_REVIEW, job_id of the deleted job) remain.

root: phpapp/lib/ops.php:5478-5487 call-delete runs only DELETE FROM jobs / DELETE FROM calls.
proposal: Refuse 'Delete call' when the call has reports, billable events, vouchers or invoices (offer Cancel instead); otherwise cascade the delete inside one transaction.

description: The 'someone else saved changes' protection does not work on a work order that has never been edited: two coordinators edit a freshly raised work order, B saves a new required date, A then saves a note from the stale page — A's save goes through and silently puts B's date back. root: phpapp/lib/ops.php:633-643 stale_edit_block() allows the save when the stored updated_at is '' ('no stored version yet → nothing to compare'), and a new call is INSERTed without updated_at (ops.php ~5938). proposal: Set updated_at = row_version_token() when a call (and a job) is created; or treat an empty posted version against a now-non-empty stored version as stale.

module: Billing / Invoicing (man-month and man-day billing units)
screen: /invoice (lines added from a job's billing units); /billunits reconciliation
description: On MySQL/MariaDB a part-month (or any quantity with 4 decimals) is rounded to 3 decimals when it goes onto the invoice, and the line amount is then recalculated from the rounded quantity. The customer is charged a different amount from what was earned. Example: 10 days of a 31-day month at Rs 1,20,000/month = 0.3226 month = Rs 38,712 earned, but the invoice line says 0.323 month = Rs 38,760 (Rs 48 too much, plus Rs 56.64 GST too much). The reconciliation then shows -48 outstanding (billed more than earned). SQLite (the test engine) stores 0.3226 and bills Rs 38,712 correctly, which is why the suite only catches it on MySQL.
steps: Fresh MariaDB 10.11 DB; tests/test_billunits_termination.php scenario 7 alone: a MANMONTH job at Rs 1,20,000 terminated after 4 months 10 days; finance adds a Rs 25,000 charge; books_line_add(invoice, job) then books_issue(invoice); billunit_reconciliation(job).
expected: Invoice subtotal Rs 5,43,712; CGST 48,934.08 + SGST 48,934.08; total Rs 6,41,580; reconciliation outstanding 0 (this is what SQLite gives).
actual: MariaDB: invoice_lines.qty = 0.323, line amount 38,760.00; invoice subtotal 5,43,760.00, CGST 48,938.40, SGST 48,938.40, total 6,41,637.00; billable_events.billed_amount 38,760 vs amount 38,712; reconciliation outstanding -48.

root: phpapp/lib/books.php:140 creates invoice_lines.qty as DECIMAL(16,3), while billing units carry qty rounded to 4 decimals (lib/billunits.php:111 round(...,4)). books_recalc() (lib/books.php:351) recomputes amount = stored qty x rate, so on MySQL the 3-decimal qty changes the money; billunit_reconcile_invoice() (lib/billunits.php:265-267) then copies the line amount into billable_events.billed_amount. screen: /contract?id=… → Approve amendment (amend-approve) on a billing-milestone amendment
description: On MySQL/MariaDB, approving an amendment that changes a contract's billing milestones can end in an error page ('There is no active transaction') even though the change has actually been saved. The app opens a transaction, then runs the milestone table set-up (CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS) inside it; MySQL silently commits the open transaction on any table set-up statement, so the later commit fails and the unguarded rollBack throws. The approver sees a crash, the amendment is in fact APPROVED and the milestones replaced, and the 'amendment APPROVED' line is not written to the quotation history. The all-or-nothing protection of this step is also lost.
steps: Fresh MariaDB DB; copy of tests/test_milestone_billing.php (unchanged logic) with, just before the amendment is applied, (1) the test's own transaction committed and (2) the per-request migration markers reset (db_epoch bumped) — this is the state of a normal live request, because index.php skips boot() when the schema fingerprint matches. Then contract_amendment_apply() as the amend-approve route calls it.
expected: Returns '' (success) — this is what SQLite does in the same simulation.
actual: MariaDB: PDOException 'There is no active transaction' escapes contract_amendment_apply() (uncaught → error page in a real request); contract_amendments.status is already APPROVED.
evidence: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Experiment-Operataion-Exaact-requirement/a8e2f8b5-ad99-5b2e-a592-b23795770424/scratchpad/a12m/ms_freshreq.php (run with /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Experiment-Operataion-Exaact-requirement/a8e2f8b5-ad99-5b2e-a592-b23795770424/scratchpad/a12m/probe_mysql.sh msfr …); output lines 'A12M: apply THREW … There is no active transaction' and 'amendment status now: APPROVED'; SQLite run: 'apply returned: '''
root: phpapp/lib/contracts.php:246 opens the transaction and calls ms_contract_replace_planned() (line 252), which calls ms_migrate() (lib/milestones.php:189 → line 40-60: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS billing_milestones, CREATE INDEX, billunit_migrate()) inside it. ms_migrate() has no 'skip while in a transaction' guard (act_migrate and connect_cap_migrate do have one), and nothing on the amend-approve route (contracts.php:1289-1307) runs ms_migrate() first. The catch at contracts.php:265 calls rollBack() without checking inTransaction().
proposal: Call ms_migrate() before beginTransaction() in contract_amendment_apply() (or give ms_migrate/billunit_migrate/books_migrate the same inTransaction() guard act_migrate has), and guard the rollBack with inTransaction(). Add a suite check that resets the migration markers before a transactional action on MySQL.
note: Found while explaining the suite crash (same MySQL behaviour: table set-up statements commit an open transaction). Reproduced by simulation of a live request in the PHP layer on local MariaDB, not by clicking through a browser on a MySQL site. The suite cannot see it because the test runner boots once and every migration marker is already set. robot/app_fix has the same contracts.php/milestones.php code paths (not re-run). Other transaction paths were only scanned, see I-A12M-01.

module: Whole app — database transactions on MySQL
what: Not every app transaction was checked for table set-up (DDL) running inside it under live-request conditions. On MySQL any CREATE/ALTER (even CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS on an existing table) silently commits an open transaction; on a live request the lazy *_migrate() markers start unset because index.php skips boot() when the schema fingerprint matches. One real case was proven (DEF-DB-002).
why: 24 transaction sites; a dynamic check needs a realistic set-up for each. Time-boxed.
attempted: Static transitive scan (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Experiment-Operataion-Exaact-requirement/a8e2f8b5-ad99-5b2e-a592-b23795770424/scratchpad/a12m/ddlreach.php) of every beginTransaction() body; manual check of the hits: ms_mark_reached (safe: ms_migrate() runs before the transaction), ops_candidates acceptance (safe: rcv_prewarm_migrations()), rver_apply and rcv_convert (safe: migrate first), connect_org_register (safe: connect_cap_migrate skips while in a transaction), act_log (safe: act_migrate skips while in a transaction), contract_amendment_apply (UNSAFE → DEF-DB-002, reproduced). Not checked dynamically: link_inspector_users (ops.php:1496 → team_member_create), ops_candidates stand-down/activate (ops.php:6704, 6781 → wf_status_move), reqversion follow-ons (hreq_apply_approved_version, crev_raise_for_version), seed_demo, backup_restore, licence buy_apply_payment, idems_next_serial. Also unguarded migrations seen: crm_migrate() runs DDL on every call even after boot (proven in test_approvals_on_dashboard / test_approval_follows_new_approver, transaction ended at their crm_migrate() line).
needed: A developer (or later agent) to add an inTransaction() guard to every *_migrate() like act_migrate has, or to run each transactional action once on MySQL after resetting the migration markers.
next: Fix DEF-DB-002 and apply the guard app-wide; then re-run the MariaDB suite with a 'fresh request' marker reset before each transactional test.

description: A branch-scoped login with no home office (e.g. a Coordinator created with Home office = —) sees EVERY branch's work orders in the work-order register, while the banner above the list tells them their lists look empty because they have no branch. Data scope fails open.

Two made-up work orders exist: ZZ-WO-AMD-1 (Ahmedabad) and ZZ-WO-MUM-1 (Mumbai). 3. Sign in as zz.nooffice → Operations → work-order counter → /calls.

root: lib/access.php:1672 call_office_clause(): `if ($off === 'ALL' || !is_array($off) || !$off) return ['1=1', []];` — an EMPTY office list returns 1=1 (every row). scope_clause() (access.php:1549) and scope_allows() already return no rows for this case via scope_needs_home(); call_office_clause() was not given the same guard. Used by the /calls register (ops.php:5497) and the dashboard open-work-orders count.
proposal: Add the same guard as scope_clause(): when $off is an empty array and scope_needs_home() is true, return ["1=0", []]. Add a guard-rail test (no-branch coordinator sees 0 calls).

root: phpapp/lib/ops.php:3588-3640 ops_module_gate(): routes 'voucher'/'vouchers' map to module 'vouchers' (ops.php:3376) and the gate refuses anyone without mod.vouchers.view; inspectors hold no module rights (access.php:928 gives them only idems edit). root: lib/company.php:149 saves capabilities only if array_key_exists(caps, $_POST); a browser sends no caps[] at all when every box is unticked, so the old set is kept.
proposal: Add a hidden caps_present=1 field to the form and save an empty set when it is present without caps[].

"hold-points" is not an access module (ACCESS_MODULES) nor covered by any product (lib/licence.php PRODUCT_MODULES), so ops_module_gate() asks can('mod.hold-points.view'), which nobody holds, and access_deny() reports it as an unavailable feature. The pop-up fires on the inbox; the snippet HTML is
. (Inside the open thread the body IS escaped.)

root: app/views/ops/connect_messages.php:51 — e(($s[last][sender_kind] === staff) ? "You: " : "") . mb_substr((string)$s[last][body], 0, 60): the closing bracket of e() is before the body, so only "You: " is escaped. The professional portal’s copy (views/pro/messages.php:63) wraps the whole expression and is safe. Same line in v52-kept and v53-kept (not fixed).
proposal: Wrap the whole snippet: e((… ? "You: " : "") . mb_substr((string)$s["last"]["body"], 0, 60)). Then search other views for e() closed before user text; consider dropping unsafe-inline from script-src.

root: phpapp/views/layout_top.php:575 `<?php foreach (take_flash() as $m): ?>` runs in the same scope as the view (index.php:777 view() extracts the view variables, then requires layout_top.php before the view), so the flash loop overwrites the view variable $m. views/ops/method_detail.php and method_form.php use $m for the method; settings.php, licence.php, crm/reports.php, preflight.php, tapi_kpi_edit.php, product_package.php also read $m and may break the same way whenever a message is shown. Same in held v52/v53.
proposal: Rename the loop variable in layout_top.php (e.g. foreach (take_flash() as $__flash)).

description: Pressing Save on a nonconformity's "Owner and date" with the boxes empty erases its due date (and owner) and says "Owner and date set." — the nonconformity then has no due date, so it can never show as overdue.
steps: Raise a TEST nonconformity (due date set automatically, e.g. 15 Dec 2026). Quality Head → open it → Owner and date → clear Owner and Due by → Save.
expected: Refused, or the existing due date kept (blank = leave as it is, as the CAPA plan form does).
actual: "Owner and date set."; nonconformities.due_on goes from 2026-12-15 to empty; History logs "ASSIGNED  by ".

root: phpapp/lib/ncr.php:597-603 ncr-assign writes trim($_POST[due_on]) straight into due_on with no empty check (compare lib/capa.php:519, which keeps the old due date when blank). Same in held v52/v53.
proposal: If due_on is blank keep the stored date (or refuse "Give it a due date — without one it can never be overdue").

proposal: Use mb_substr(…, 0, N, "UTF-8") for user text.

steps: Consents → Their name "TEST Asha Mehta", purpose "TEST purpose" → Record. Then Their name "TEST Ravi", same purpose → Record.
expected: Two consent rows, one per person.

evidence: SCR-consents step 7 (re-check); robot shots/SCR-consents-7-redo.jpg
root: phpapp/lib/compliance.php:993-995 consent_record() treats an existing live row with the same subject_kind + subject_id + purpose as a duplicate; people typed by name all have subject_id 0, so every later person with that purpose matches the first row and nothing is inserted (and the caller still flashes success). Same in held v52/v53.
proposal: When subject_id is 0 include subject_name in the duplicate test (or drop the dedupe for name-only entries), and tell the user when an existing consent was found instead of claiming a new one was recorded.
note: Personal-data register (DPDP). Also SCR-consent-add / SCR-consent-withdraw step 7. Approval flagged because consent records are a data-protection control.

root: phpapp/lib/identity.php:651-655 stores the ticks only if array_key_exists(person_req_docs, $_POST); a browser sends no key when every box is unticked, so the __NONE__ sentinel is never written and person_req_docs() (:80-86) falls back to the defaults. proposal: Add a hidden person_req_docs_present=1 field and treat its presence with no ticks as "none required"; cap retention days at a sensible maximum.

description: The client portal's payment-confirmation address accepts ANY marketplace order number and, when the signature is wrong, marks that order FAILED — even when the order belongs to another client. A signed-in client who knows (or obtains) another client's Razorpay order id can spoil that client's pending plan/credit-pack payment.
steps: Private copy, no Razorpay keys. Two PENDING plan orders in mkt_orders: order_TBfakeRefinery01 (TB Refinery) and order_TBfakeSteel0001 (TB Steel Works). Sign in to the portal as TB Refinery Main → POST /portal/pay with razorpay_order_id=order_TBfakeSteel0001, a made-up payment id and signature.
expected: The other client's order is not touched (the confirmation is only accepted for the signed-in client's own order).
actual: TB Steel Works' order changed PENDING → FAILED with payment_id 'pay_TBfake2'. If TB Steel Works were paying at that moment, its real Razorpay callback would then be told 'already processed, or the order is unknown' — money taken, plan not activated.
evidence: robot results/CP-011.json step 5; shots/CP-011-5-fail.jpg; database mkt_orders row
root: lib/portal.php:1020-1026 (portal/pay POST) calls mkt_pay_verify() without the signed-in party; lib/mkt_pay.php:138-145 mkt_pay_verify() looks the order up by order_id only and writes FAILED on a bad signature. The GET side (mkt_pay_order($id,'CLIENT',$party)) IS scoped. Practical risk is limited because Razorpay order ids are long random strings. Same code in the held v53 copy ($R/app_fix) — not fixed there.
files: phpapp/lib/portal.php, phpapp/lib/mkt_pay.php (same pattern on /pro/pay in lib/connect_pro.php:858)
proposal: Pass the subscriber kind + id into mkt_pay_verify() and only consider an order WHERE subscriber_kind=? AND subscriber_id=?; do not mark an order FAILED on a signature mismatch coming from a browser (leave it PENDING and log the attempt).
note: Not fixed in held v52/v53 (mkt_pay_verify unchanged in app_fix).

description: At the Super Admin address, a COMPANY account signing in with its correct e-mail and password is told "Invalid username or password." instead of "This address is only for the platform owner (Super Admin). Company users sign in at https://<main>/login." (a member of the platform owner's own staff does get the right sentence).
steps: Platform setup → Super Admin address = opsadmin.a14.test → open http://opsadmin.a14.test/login → sign in as a company owner (door@a14.test) with the right password.
expected: "This address is only for the platform owner (Super Admin). Company users sign in at https://ops.a14.test/login."
actual: "Invalid username or password." — the person thinks their password is wrong.
evidence: robot shots/PLT-004-5-fail.jpg
root: phpapp/index.php ~930: on the admin host the e-mail is never routed to its company (saas_login_lookup skipped), so the password is checked against the control users table and fails before the wrong-door check at ~966.
proposal: On the Super Admin address, when an e-mail belongs to a company in the directory, answer with superadmin_wrong_door_msg() (without checking or revealing the password).

description: When Add a company is refused (e.g. workspace key already taken), the page reloads with the red message but the "＋ Add a company" panel is CLOSED, so the entries the platform owner typed look lost until they open the panel again (they are kept inside it).
steps: Companies → ＋ Add a company → Company "Admin", key "admin", owner, e-mail, plan → Create company.
expected: Everything typed is still in the form (visible) and the key box is outlined in red.
actual: Message "That workspace key is already taken — pick another. \"admin-2\" is free." shown; the form is folded away; reopening shows the entries kept and the key box red.
evidence: robot shots/PLT-004-10-fail.jpg (earlier run), PLT-004-10.jpg
root: phpapp/views/ops/saas_companies.php:44 — <details class="sc-card"> has no `open` attribute when a draft ($_SESSION['company_add_draft']) is being shown.
proposal: Render the details element with `open` whenever a company_add_draft exists.

description: The application form silently cuts long input: a 300-character company name is stored as 150 characters and a 5,000-character note as 500; the page says "Request received" with no word that text was dropped.
steps: /get-started → Company name 300 characters, note 5,000 characters → Request my workspace →.
expected: Saved, or refused with a sentence (never silent loss).
actual: Saved; company 150 chars, note 500 chars; the rest silently dropped.

root: phpapp/lib/tenant_signup.php ~126 mb_substr($company,0,150) / mb_substr($note,0,500) with no maxlength on the boxes and no message.
proposal: Put maxlength=150 / 500 on the boxes (browser shows the limit) and refuse over-long input with a sentence.

expected: Profile saved; the card reads Complete; bought modules stay as they are.

screen: /companies → Manage → Modules this company has bought; company /workspace/setup/modules
description: "Modules this company has bought" does not change what the company is entitled to — the plan does. Unticking modules only hides them: a Professional company reduced to Sales & CRM sees Operations, Money and People & hiring as "Off · In your plan — turn it on when you need it" and its owner can switch Operations back on ("Operations is now on." → the work-order register opens) without paying. The reverse also happens (ONB-043): Marketplace & Connect ticked and saved for an Enterprise company shows "🔒 Not in plan" inside the company. The not-bought pages say "switched off for this workspace" instead of "isn’t included in your current subscription".
steps: Companies → TB Sales Only (Professional) → tick only Sales & CRM → Save modules → owner: Admin → Modules & features → Operations → Add this to my workspace → /calls.
expected: Every module not bought shows "🔒 Not in plan" with "Upgrade to add it" and no switch; /calls shows "Operations isn’t included in your current subscription."
actual: Only 2 modules locked; Operations/Money/People & hiring switchable; switching Operations on opens the Inspection call register. Marketplace bought for TB All Co stays locked.
evidence: robot shots/ONB-041-3-fail.jpg, ONB-041-4-fail.jpg, ONB-043-2-fail.jpg, ONB-043-3-fail.jpg
root: Company modules push (lib/saas_tenants.php do=company_modules → saas_tenant_set_modules/saas_push_to_tenant) sets visibility, while the tenant's entitlement (saas_entitled_modules / plan PRO/ENTERPRISE) still decides 'in plan' in the cockpit (views/ops/cockpit_modules.php 'locked').
proposal: Make Save modules write the company's entitlement (saas_entitled_modules) to exactly the ticked list, so un-bought modules are locked and bought ones are unlocked.

description: A DRAFT inspection report that was never submitted, reviewed or approved can be finalised & issued (locked, client e-mailed) by any holder of idems.finalize (Senior Inspector, Branch Manager …) by sending the Finalize form. The screen hides the button, but the server only checks the approval chain when one exists — a never-submitted report has none — so DRAFT → ISSUED goes through, skipping the completeness gate and approval. docs/03 allows only APPROVED → ISSUED.
steps: 1) Inspector: New inspection report for a work order (IR), Generate — status Draft, not filled, not submitted. 2) Senior Inspector opens it: no 'Finalize & issue' button. 3) Senior Inspector sends the finalize form (an old page / crafted request: POST /document-finalize?id=<id> with the page's CSRF token).
expected: Refused: 'This report must be submitted and fully approved before it can be issued' (only APPROVED → ISSUED, docs/03-object-lifecycles.md 'Inspection report').
actual: HTTP 200 'Report MGH/AHM/2026/TBREFI/IR/000001 finalized & issued. It is now locked (immutable). The client has been notified (1 recipient).' — status ISSUED, finalized=1 by Test SrInspector, submitted_at and approved_by empty; audit FINALIZE + CLIENT_NOTIFIED; e-mail 'Your inspection report … is ready' queued to the client. Seen first in FLOW-01 (a script slip sent the finalize before the report was submitted) and reproduced on a clean copy. An Inspector (no idems.finalize) is refused.
evidence: robot a16/shots/DEV-repro1-issued.jpg; DB report_docs + idems_audit on q_a16b
root: phpapp/lib/idems.php:4887-4904 (document-finalize): the status test is inside `if ($hasChain && $doc['status'] !== 'APPROVED' && !is_master())` — with no report_approvals rows ($hasChain = 0) the status is never checked; the button gate in views/ops/idems/doc_detail.php:15/43 ($canFinalize = anyApproved && !anyPending) is screen-only. Same code in the held app_fix copy (idems.php:4901).
proposal: In document-finalize refuse unless status === 'APPROVED' (keep the master override only if the owner wants it, with a recorded reason), independent of whether an approval chain exists; also run idems_completeness_check() server-side at finalize.

module: Operations → Money (hand-over work order → deputation → profitability)
description: A monthly deputation allocated on a man-month work order is saved with a value of the man-month rate × the number of visit DAYS instead of × the months. The allocation form itself says '120,172.5 per man-month × 6 = 721035.00', but the saved deputation is worth ₹1,86,26,737.50 (155 working days × ₹1,20,172.50), and the Contract number register shows PROFIT ₹18,626,738 (100% margin) for a contract worth ₹7.21 L before tax.
steps: FLOW-02: approved costing → man-month quotation (6 × ₹1,20,172.50 = ₹7,21,035) → accepted → contract opened → New work order from that quote/line (billable basis Man-month, rate ₹1,20,172.50) → '+ Allocate': Type = Resident / site posting (also with Day-based inspection), engineer, Order & dates: Monthly job, months 6 → Money tab shows '… per man-month × 6 = 721035.00' → 'Allocate & send email'.
expected: Deputation value = 6 × ₹1,20,172.50 = ₹7,21,035 (what the form showed and what was sold).
actual: jobs.invoice_value = 18626737.5; job_visits = 155 (02 Nov 2026 – 30 Apr 2027, 6-day weeks); Money → Contract number register row 'AHM/C/2026-27/00001 … PROFIT INR ₹18,626,738 · 100%'. Same result with job type 'Day-based inspection'.
evidence: robot a16/shots/DEV-DEF-FLOW-002-profitability.jpg, robot a16/shots/DEV-DEF-FLOW-002-job.jpg; FLOW-02 step 16
root: phpapp/lib/ops.php:8298-8305 (job save): when invoice_value_auto, invoice_value = call.billable_rate × mandays, and with mandays empty the quantity becomes count(visit dates) — the call's billable_basis (MANMONTH) and the job's months_count are ignored; the browser computes rate × months, so the screen and the stored figure disagree. Same code in the held app_fix copy.
proposal: On save, compute the quantity from the billing basis: MANMONTH → months_count (or the man-month units the schedule spans); MANDAY → man-days/visit days; VISIT → visits; LOT → 1. Never overwrite a value the form showed without telling the user; add a server test for a 6-month man-month deputation.
note: Not in the V51 defect list; same code in the held app_fix copy. Billing itself (man-month billing units / timesheet events) does not use this figure, but Profit by work order, the Contract number register and the job's own revenue do.

root: lib/reqversion.php:1222-1250 rver_gate_requisition_edit() treats the form's defaults (req_type "NEW", min_experience_years 0) as changes against stored blanks/NULL, and asks for $_POST[change_reason]; views/ops/requisition_form.php has no change_reason input (grep: 0). screen: Money → Billing workspace (/to-bill) → 'Draft invoice for the ticked work'
description: An invoice drafted from the Billing workspace loses the client's terms and the contract: credit days 0 (so the due date = the invoice date), payment terms blank and the header 'CONTRACT —' (also missing on the print), although the client record has 60 credit days / 'Against invoice' and the job and the line carry the contract number. '+ New invoice' carries them ('carry' from the client), so the two doors give different invoices for the same work.
steps: FLOW-12: client ZZ FLOW12 Ltd with Payment terms 'Against invoice', Credit days 60; a closed ₹1,00,000 job on contract TEST-CN-…. Finance → Billable events → Sync → Approve → Billing workspace → tick the job → 'Draft invoice for the ticked work' → 'Issue this invoice'. (Same in FLOW-01 step 29 for the contract number.)
expected: Due date = invoice date + 60 days (15 Jan 2027 for a 16 Nov 2026 invoice); payment terms 'Against invoice'; Contract number = the job's contract (shown on the invoice and its print).
actual: Invoice AHM/2627/0001 ₹1,18,000 'ZZ FLOW12 Ltd · 16 Nov 2026 · due 16 Nov 2026'; invoices.credit_days 0, payment_terms '', contract_number ''; FLOW-01: 'This invoice bills … CONTRACT —' and the print view has no contract number. The ageing therefore treats the invoice as due on the day it is raised.
evidence: robot a16/shots/FLOW-12-1-fail.jpg, FLOW-01-29-fail.jpg; DB invoices on q_a16b / q_a16a
root: phpapp/views/ops/to_bill.php:36-44 posts only partner_id, jobs[] and only to /invoice-new; lib/books.php:565-568 books_invoice_create() takes credit_days/due_date/payment_terms/contract_number only from the POST (books_carry_for() is used for the '+ New invoice' form only, lib/booksui.php:268-276). Same in the held app_fix copy.
proposal: When the draft is started from the Billing workspace, fill credit days, payment terms, PO and (single-contract) contract number from books_carry_for(partner, jobs) exactly as '+ New invoice' does, and compute the due date from them.
note: Not in the V51 defect list. Amounts and GST are correct; only terms, due date and contract reference are lost.

module: Directory / Money (hand-over receipts → Customer 360 money timeline)
description: The Customer 360 'Money timeline' understates money received but not yet matched whenever a customer withheld TDS: it subtracts every allocation (cash AND TDS) from the cash received. With ₹1,19,000 received, ₹1,16,000 cash + ₹2,000 TDS matched and ₹3,000 left unmatched, the timeline says 'RECEIVED, NOT YET MATCHED ₹1,000' while the card at the top of the same page and the Money in register say ₹3,000.
steps: FLOW-12: invoice ₹1,18,000; receipts ₹50,000 (matched), ₹66,000 + TDS ₹2,000 (matched), ₹3,000 (not matched). Finance → Directory → ZZ FLOW12 Ltd → 360.
expected: Money timeline 'Received, not yet matched' ₹3,000 (same as the ₹3,000 card and Money in → 'Not yet matched' / 'Left to match ₹3,000').
actual: Top card '₹3,000 RECEIVED, NOT YET MATCHED'; Money timeline 'RECEIVED ₹1.19 L · OUTSTANDING ₹0 · RECEIVED, NOT YET MATCHED ₹1,000'.
evidence: robot a16/shots/FLOW-12-11*.jpg; DB receipts / receipt_allocations on q_a16b
root: phpapp/lib/finevent.php:113-114 — unmatched = received (cash receipts) − financial_allocated(), and financial_allocated() (finevent.php:120-131) sums receipt_allocations of every kind including TDS, which is not cash received.
proposal: Compare like with like: unmatched = (cash received + TDS recorded on the receipts) − all allocations, or subtract only CASH allocations from cash received.
note: Not in the V51 defect list (DEF-FIN-008 is the home-screen chip, a different screen and cause).
